quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #19
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: What should you do if you have a tire blowout?

options.text: Take your foot off the gas.
Do not use your brakes right away.
Slowly reduce speed and pull to the side of the road.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: If you have a tire blowout, take your foot off the gas pedal. Do not brake immediately. Slowly reduce your speed, then gently apply the brakes and pull to the side of the road.

questions.question: Distracted driving is:

options.text: Very rare.
Very dangerous.
Not a problem.
Just as safe as normal driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Very dangerous.
questions.explanation: Distracted driving is very dangerous. It puts you, your passengers, pedestrians, cyclists, and other drivers at risk. Paying full attention to the road helps prevent crashes.

questions.question: Your vehicle is blocking traffic after an accident. What should you do?

options.text: Move your vehicle off the road if you can.
Do not move your vehicle under any circumstances.
Wait for police to arrive before moving your vehicle.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move your vehicle off the road if you can.
questions.explanation: After a minor accident, move your vehicle off the road if possible. Do not leave the scene without giving your information and offering help if needed.

questions.question: What does a steady green light mean?

options.text: You must slow down and be ready to stop.
You must stop and look before going.
You may go through if the road is clear.
You cannot turn right.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may go through if the road is clear.
questions.explanation: A steady green light means you can drive through the intersection if the road is clear. You can also turn right or left on green unless a sign says you cannot. Always yield to other cars and pedestrians when turning.

questions.question: When should your wheels NOT point straight ahead?

options.text: While waiting to turn left at a traffic light.
When parked on a hill or sloped driveway.
When parked on a flat road with no curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: When parked on a hill or sloped driveway.
questions.explanation: When waiting to turn left, keep your wheels straight. This protects you if hit from behind. When parked on a hill or slope, angle your wheels so the car won't roll into traffic if the brakes fail.

questions.question: A steady yellow traffic light means what color light is coming next?

options.text: Flashing yellow
Steady green
Steady red
Flashing red

questions.correctAnswerText: Steady red
questions.explanation: A steady yellow light means a steady red light will appear next.

questions.question: When must you yield to emergency vehicles?

options.text: Never.
When you see flashing red or blue lights or hear a siren.
Only when other vehicles yield.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see flashing red or blue lights or hear a siren.
questions.explanation: You must yield to any emergency vehicle that has flashing lights or a siren on.

questions.question: How should you watch the road to be ready for dangers ahead?

options.text: Look at the whole road and both sides.
Look straight ahead only.
Rest your left foot lightly on the brake pedal while driving.
Focus on the middle of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look at the whole road and both sides.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle dangerous situations is to spot problems early. Look far ahead, but also scan the entire road including the sides. Do not just stare straight ahead.

questions.question: When passing a large vehicle in a small car, what should you expect?

options.text: Loud noise.
Heavy pollution.
Strong wind from the large vehicle.
Falling parts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Strong wind from the large vehicle.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles create strong wind gusts that can push smaller cars. Be ready to steer carefully when passing or meeting large vehicles at high speeds.

questions.question: How do you avoid losing grip on wet roads?

options.text: Make sharp turns.
Press the brakes hard.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: To avoid losing grip on wet roads, reduce your speed and keep your tires in good condition. If you lose control, take your foot off the gas and do not brake. Keep your car straight and let it slow down naturally.

questions.question: At night, how should you look to reduce headlight glare from oncoming cars?

options.text: Straight ahead.
Over your shoulder.
At the center of the road.
To the right edge of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: To the right edge of the road.
questions.explanation: If an oncoming driver does not dim their headlights, watch the right side of the road ahead. Do not look directly at the bright headlights. The glare can blind you for several seconds.

questions.question: What do drivers need to do on interstate highways?

options.text: Be able to safely drive at higher speeds.
Stay alert at all times.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Safe interstate driving requires you to stay alert and be able to drive at high speeds.

questions.question: You are driving at the speed limit when the traffic light turns yellow. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down and drive through without looking both ways.
Speed up to cross before the light turns red.
Stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means the red light is coming. Stop at a yellow light if you can do so safely. If you cannot stop safely, cross the intersection carefully.

questions.question: Your vehicle has a problem and you need to make an emergency stop. What should you do?

options.text: Honk your horn to warn other drivers.
Get out of the vehicle once you stop.
Turn on your emergency flashers and stay in your vehicle if you can.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your emergency flashers and stay in your vehicle if you can.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle breaks down, get off the road and away from traffic if possible. Turn on your emergency flashers. Stay inside your vehicle to protect yourself from traffic.

questions.question: What does a flashing yellow light at an intersection mean?

options.text: Slow down and proceed with caution.
Come to a complete stop as fast as possible.
Stop and proceed only when the intersection is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down and be careful. You do not need to stop completely at a flashing yellow light.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No U-turn.
No turning.
No left turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot make a U-turn. You cannot turn around to go in the opposite direction at this location.

questions.question: What should you do when driving in fog?

options.text: Turn on your high beam headlights.
Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
Speed up so you do not cause an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: In fog, slow down and use your low beam lights. If the fog is too thick and you cannot see, pull off the road and wait for it to clear.

questions.question: When must you show proof of insurance to a police officer?

options.text: Only if you are in a collision.
If you are in a collision or stopped for a ticket.
Only if you are stopped and given a ticket.

questions.correctAnswerText: If you are in a collision or stopped for a ticket.
questions.explanation: You must carry proof of insurance at all times. Show your proof of insurance and license to an officer when asked after a traffic stop or collision.

questions.question: Your tire suddenly goes flat while driving. What should you do?

options.text: Pump the brake pedal several times quickly.
Slow down gradually without braking hard.
Press the brake pedal down as hard as you can.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually without braking hard.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat, grip the steering wheel firmly and keep the vehicle straight. Take your foot off the gas. Do not brake hard. Let the vehicle slow on its own and use the brakes gently if needed. Pull off the road when it is safe.

questions.question: Hydroplaning happens when:

options.text: Your windshield wipers cannot clear the rain.
Your tires lose contact with the road.
Spray from a truck blocks your vision.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your tires lose contact with the road.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning occurs when you drive too fast on a wet surface and your tires lose all contact with the road. Your vehicle slides on top of the water instead of gripping the road.

questions.question: You exit the freeway on a ramp that curves downhill. You should:

options.text: Slow down to a safe speed before entering the curve.
Slow down to the posted freeway speed limit.
Wait until you are in the curve to start braking.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to a safe speed before entering the curve.
questions.explanation: Always slow down before entering a curve. You cannot see what is ahead, and braking in a curve may cause your vehicle to skid.

questions.question: When entering a roundabout, you should slow down and:

options.text: Yield to pedestrians and bicyclists crossing.
Yield to cars already in the roundabout.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: When entering a roundabout, yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and cars already in the roundabout.

questions.question: What does a single dashed white line between lanes mean?

options.text: You may pass even if it is dangerous.
Traffic in these lanes moves in opposite directions.
You may not pass.
You may pass if it is safe to do so.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may pass if it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: White lines separate lanes moving in the same direction. Dashed white lines can be crossed to pass or change lanes if it is safe.

questions.question: A broken yellow centerline means:

options.text: Passing is not allowed.
You may pass on the right when the road ahead is clear.
You may pass on the left when the road ahead is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may pass on the left when the road ahead is clear.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow centerline means you can cross it to pass another vehicle on the left if no oncoming traffic is coming. Never cross a solid yellow centerline to pass.

questions.question: Use extra caution when driving near a pedestrian with a white cane because:

options.text: The person is deaf.
The person is a police officer.
The person is blind.
The person has poor balance.

questions.correctAnswerText: The person is blind.
questions.explanation: A white cane or guide dog means a pedestrian is blind. You must slow down, yield, and proceed with caution. Be ready to stop to avoid hitting them.

questions.question: Driving too fast:

options.text: Does not increase crash risk.
Helps you react faster to danger.
Often leads to poor and risky decisions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Often leads to poor and risky decisions.
questions.explanation: Speeding is a major cause of crashes. It does not save time and often leads to risky decisions.

questions.question: When driving on slippery surfaces like snow or ice:

options.text: Shift to a low gear before going down steep hills.
Stay close to the car ahead to maintain traction.
Pump your brakes to prevent them from freezing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift to a low gear before going down steep hills.
questions.explanation: To avoid skidding on slippery surfaces, shift to a low gear before steep hills. Stay farther behind other vehicles than normal. Avoid sudden stops. If you don't have antilock brakes, pump the brakes gently to slow down.

questions.question: Your wheels slip off the road edge while driving. You should:

options.text: Jerk the steering wheel to force the vehicle back onto the road.
Speed up and gradually steer back onto the road.
Slam on the brakes and stop.
Gently use the brakes to slow down. Turn the wheel gradually to return to the road at a safe speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gently use the brakes to slow down. Turn the wheel gradually to return to the road at a safe speed.
questions.explanation: If your wheels leave the road, keep them off the pavement and slow down gently with the brakes. Once at a safe speed, turn the wheel to get back on the road. Do not jerk the wheel sharply.

questions.question: When entering traffic from a parked position at the curb, you should:

options.text: Drive slower than other traffic for 200 feet.
Wait for a large gap so you can speed up to match other traffic.
Wait for the first two cars to pass, then pull in.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for a large gap so you can speed up to match other traffic.
questions.explanation: When merging into traffic, wait for a gap large enough to reach the speed of the other vehicles.

questions.question: You are waiting to turn left at a multilane intersection, and oncoming traffic blocks your view. You should:

options.text: Accelerate quickly when the first lane is clear.
Wait until you can see all lanes you need to cross before turning.
Wait for an oncoming driver to wave you across.
Slowly move into each lane as it clears.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until you can see all lanes you need to cross before turning.
questions.explanation: Never start a left turn until you can see all lanes are clear and you can turn safely.

questions.question: You are driving behind a motorcycle and want to pass. What must you do?

options.text: Stay in the right lane because the motorcycle is small and does not take up the whole lane.
Honk your horn to make the motorcycle move to the shoulder so you can pass.
Keep your vehicle fully in the left lane before you pass and while you pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your vehicle fully in the left lane before you pass and while you pass.
questions.explanation: When passing a motorcycle, give the motorcycle a full lane. Do not share the same lane with the motorcycle. If you move back to your lane too soon, the rider may have to swerve right into traffic or off the road.

questions.question: A red arrow on a traffic light means:

options.text: You must drive slowly through the intersection.
You must stop, then go when it is safe.
You must stop, then go when the light turns green or a green arrow appears.
You may turn in the direction the red arrow points.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must stop, then go when the light turns green or a green arrow appears.
questions.explanation: Unless a sign says otherwise, a red arrow means you must stop completely. You must stay stopped until a green light or green arrow appears.

questions.question: Which of the following affects how fast your body absorbs alcohol?

options.text: Weight
Height
Intelligence

questions.correctAnswerText: Weight
questions.explanation: How fast your body absorbs alcohol depends on your weight, biological sex, how much food is in your stomach, and how many drinks you have had. The only way to remove alcohol from your system is to wait.

questions.question: Which statement is true about seat belts and child restraints?

options.text: Never place a baby or small child in the front seat of a vehicle with airbags.
An airbag can hurt a baby or small child, even in a slow crash.
Always make sure all passengers wear a seat belt or use a child restraint.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Before driving, fasten your seat belt and make sure all passengers use seat belts or child restraints. Seat belts greatly reduce the chance of being hurt or killed in a crash. Children 12 and under should ride properly restrained in a back seat. Never put a rear-facing baby seat in the front seat of a vehicle with a front airbag.

questions.question: Which road surface freezes first?

options.text: A tunnel
An intersection
A bridge

questions.correctAnswerText: A bridge
questions.explanation: Bridges and overpasses freeze before other roads and thaw out after other roads. A bridge can ice over even when nearby roads are dry.

questions.question: A green arrow on a lane control signal means:

options.text: You may use this lane.
No traffic is allowed in this lane.
You have the right-of-way.
You must merge into this lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may use this lane.
questions.explanation: A steady green arrow pointing down over a lane means you may drive in that lane.

questions.question: When you see an octagonal sign, you must:

options.text: Slow down.
Stop.
Turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: An octagonal (eight-sided) sign always means "Stop." Come to a complete stop, yield to traffic and people with the right-of-way, and go when the way is clear.

questions.question: When you see a flashing red traffic light, you should:

options.text: Drive through if no other cars are coming.
Keep driving because you have the right-of-way.
Stop only if a police officer is nearby.
Treat it like a stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat it like a stop sign.
questions.explanation: Flashing red lights are used at dangerous intersections. Treat them the same as a stop sign.

questions.question: When riding in a vehicle, small children:

options.text: Can be safely held by a strong adult.
Will be safe if they stand on the floor in the back.
Will not be hurt in an accident because they are small.
Must never stand while the vehicle is moving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must never stand while the vehicle is moving.
questions.explanation: Special child seats are made for small children. No person is strong enough to hold a child safely during a crash or sudden stop. Always have children properly fastened in a seat.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, when should you return to your original lane?

options.text: When you can see both headlights of the other vehicle in your rearview mirror.
When you have cleared the front bumper of the other vehicle.
When you are 50 feet ahead of the other vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see both headlights of the other vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: When passing, move back into your lane only when you can see the other vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror. This means you have enough space to safely move in front of the other vehicle.

questions.question: How often should you check your rearview mirror while driving?

options.text: Every two to four seconds
Every four to six seconds
Every six to eight seconds
Every eight to ten seconds

questions.correctAnswerText: Every six to eight seconds
questions.explanation: Check your rearview mirror every six to eight seconds to see traffic behind you.

questions.question: You must obey school crossing guards:

options.text: At all times.
Only during school hours.
Unless you do not see any children present.

questions.correctAnswerText: At all times.
questions.explanation: Always obey crossing guards near schools. Stay alert and follow their instructions.

questions.question: Alcohol in any amount is:

options.text: A stimulant.
A depressant.
Neither of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: A depressant.
questions.explanation: Alcohol is a depressant. It slows your nerve impulses and body functions. It reduces your focus and alertness.

questions.question: If your tires feel like they have lost grip on the road, you should:

options.text: Slow down by shifting into a lower gear.
Ease your foot off the gas pedal.
Slow down by pumping the brakes quickly and firmly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ease your foot off the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: Ease off the gas pedal and stay off the brakes. Do not stop or turn until your tires grip the road again.

questions.question: What does this road sign indicate?

options.text: Directions for children
School zone ahead
Playground area ahead

questions.correctAnswerText: School zone ahead
questions.explanation: Pentagon signs warn you about school zones or school crossings. Watch for children and follow the posted speed limits.

questions.question: Before entering a curve, you should:

options.text: Activate your turn signal.
Reduce your speed.
Brake hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed.
questions.explanation: Slow down before curves where you cannot see ahead. Other reasons to reduce speed include slippery roads, hills, and areas with animals or pedestrians.

questions.question: Stopping distances and crash severity:

options.text: Decrease as vehicle speed increases.
Are not affected by vehicle speed.
Increase as vehicle speed increases.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase as vehicle speed increases.
questions.explanation: Higher speeds require longer stopping distances and cause more severe crashes.

questions.question: If the road ahead is flooded, you should:

options.text: Slam on the brakes.
Not drive through the flooded area. Turn around and find another route.
Drive only in the center of the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not drive through the flooded area. Turn around and find another route.
questions.explanation: Never drive through flooded roads. Water may hide hazards. Turn around and use a different route.

questions.question: If you need to stop quickly and your vehicle does not have an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS), you should:

options.text: Hold down the brake pedal.
Firmly pump your brakes.
Lightly tap the brakes.
Release the brake pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Firmly pump your brakes.
questions.explanation: Pump the brakes firmly in an emergency. This stops your car quickly and lets you keep steering control.

questions.question: You may cross double yellow lines to pass another vehicle if the:

options.text: Vehicle in front of you moves to the right to let you pass.
Yellow line next to your side of the road is broken.
Yellow line next to the opposite side of the road is broken.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow line next to your side of the road is broken.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line on your side means you can pass if it is safe. A solid yellow line means you cannot pass.
